external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches to the self-hosted git server and can manually start a rebuild of main on the build runner.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand; that path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
external_entities.notes: The source does not identify the operator or technology of the public package registry.

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be used by developers to start a rebuild of main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on dependencies downloaded during resolution.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: A controller that holds the current image SHA for the estate and responds to store server queries about the current release.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The source does not state what a store server presents to the controller.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in a store back office that runs the till software as a container, checks the current release, pulls a changed image, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: The source describes about 1,200 stores but does not distinguish individual store servers.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container
processes.notes: The source does not describe the till software's interfaces or technology.

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: A self-hosted git server on the corporate network containing developer branches and the source used for builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: A registry in the build environment containing finished container images tagged with commit SHAs and available for store server pulls.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows the pull, but the source does not state what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: start build
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build on the build runner.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: kick rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: Finished container image tagged with commit SHA

data_flows.name: make release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: query release
data_flows.description: A store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull, but the source does not state what a store server presents to it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network containing the git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The in-store estate containing the store servers and till software.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Build and deploy pipeline for the in-store estate.
trust_boundaries.notes: The source says the image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: retail WAN
trust_boundaries.description: The WAN over which traffic between the stores and corporate network travels.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The developer is assigned to the corporate network because the source does not state a separate developer network while describing the developer's interactions with the corporate build infrastructure.
assumptions.basis: The description places the git server and deploy controller on the corporate network but does not state where developers connect from.
